label: Skill Management
title: Skill Management
subtitle: The authoring surface for skills: list what already exists, inspect how one is written, create a new skill from markdown instructions, and delete a skill that is no longer wanted.
whenToUse: Used when a way of working should outlive one conversation. An agent that has just worked out a procedure can write it down as a skill, so any agent the skill is assigned to picks up the same procedure in a later project. Inspecting an existing skill first is the fastest way to learn the house style before writing a new one.

methods.name: Create Skill
methods.description: Creates a skill from a name, a human-facing description, an agent-facing description, and the markdown instructions. Files already in the project — text like references and scripts, or binary like a PowerPoint deck or an image — can be bundled into the skill by naming their paths; they are copied in alongside the instructions. Every skill is global — there is no way to scope one to a single project — and it becomes usable once it is assigned to an agent in Settings.

methods.name: Inspect Skill
methods.description: Copies a skill's folder — the instructions, the manifest, and every bundled file — into the project folder, where the Filesystem tool can read them. Use it to see how an existing skill is written. The copy is a scratch snapshot: inspecting the same skill again replaces it.

methods.name: Delete Skill
methods.description: Deletes a skill created by a user. Skills that came from the marketplace are read-only and stay untouched.

methods.name: List Skills
methods.description: Lists every skill on the platform — its id, whether it is switched on, and whether it can be deleted. A listed skill still has to be assigned to an agent in Settings before that agent can use it.
